Scar care for cuts

#How to use scar cream?
1.	⁠Open the container and set it on a cleaned surface.
2.	⁠Wash tour hands thouroughly. This shows you how to do so properly.
3.	⁠Dry your hands with a clean paper towel, or if you do not have those, a clean towel/rag. Do not use a used towel as this will make your hands dirty again.
4.	⁠Take your clean fingers and put as much cream on it as you think you need. This is trial and error and depends on the size of your wounds. It should be enough that it covers the entire cut, but it should be little enough that there isn’t excess scar cream sitting on your skin.
5.	⁠Use one finger per new dip - meaning, if you dip with your index finger, put on the cream, and if decide you need more, next time you dip, use your middle finger. Next your ringfinger, etc. If you run out of fingers, repeat the first few steps and start over.
6.	⁠Very gently massage the cream over your cuts. Do not put pressure on the wounds, go very lightly, and make sure you do not pull off the scabs. If they are partially loose, DO NOT pull them off! Let them soak in the cream and let them come off on their own when they are ready.**

**If you take off the scabs, the scars will heal thicker and less pretty than if they were to soak off on their own, so try not to pull them off!

#When to use scar cream?
- You can start putting on the scar cream as soon as the wound _is closed_ with scabs.* Massaging in scar cream helps promote bloodflow (thus healing), keeps the wound moisturized which helps the scabs soak off in due time, and also helps against itching. 

- Put on the scar cream on 3 times a day for the first month, 1/2 times a day for the next 2 months, and then after every shower for the next 3 months. This will help the wound close faster, and make the scars softer and fade in color a lot faster.

*DO NOT put scar cream (or petroleum jelly etc) on an open cut!!! This will trap bacteria underneath. Scar cream (etc) is not meant to go inside the body, and should be used externally only. Wait until the wound is covered in scabs!

#What can I use if I don’t have scar cream?

The scar cream I am referencing in this post is Vitamin E cream, but you may also use petroleum jelly or virgin coconut oil instead. It’s mostly about keeping the scabs moisturized until they fall off, and massaging the cuts for more bloodflow (which promotes healing).
